flashcard_questions.q: Why are the noble gases unreactive?
flashcard_questions.a: They already have full outer shells of electrons.

flashcard_questions.q: Between which two types of element does ionic bonding occur?
What happens to electrons during ionic bonding?
flashcard_questions.a: They transfer from the metal atom to the non-metal atom.

flashcard_questions.q: What holds an ionic compound together?
flashcard_questions.a: Strong electrostatic attraction between oppositely charged ions.

flashcard_questions.q: Why does a metal atom become a positively charged ion?
flashcard_questions.a: It loses electrons, so it then has more protons than electrons.

flashcard_questions.q: How many outer electrons does a sodium atom transfer to chlorine?
Between which type of atoms does covalent bonding occur?
What is a single covalent bond?
flashcard_questions.a: One shared pair of electrons between two atoms.

flashcard_questions.q: How many pairs of electrons are shared in a double bond?
Which type of bond joins the two atoms in a nitrogen molecule?
flashcard_questions.a: A triple bond, sharing three pairs of electrons.

flashcard_questions.q: What is a lone pair of electrons?
flashcard_questions.a: A pair in an atom's outer shell that is not involved in bonding.

flashcard_questions.q: What are delocalised electrons in a metal?
flashcard_questions.a: Electrons free to move throughout the whole metal structure.

flashcard_questions.q: How is the structure of a metal described in metallic bonding?
flashcard_questions.a: A regular lattice of positive ions surrounded by a sea of delocalised electrons.

flashcard_questions.q: Why do metals generally have high melting and boiling points?
flashcard_questions.a: A lot of energy is needed to overcome the strong electrostatic forces.

flashcard_questions.q: Why do ionic compounds conduct electricity when molten but not when solid?
flashcard_questions.a: Molten ions are free to move and carry charge; solid ions are fixed.

notes: 15 cards: 5 term to definition, 5 why/what-happens-if, 3 structure to function (ionic lattice, metallic lattice, delocalised electrons), 2 counting cards for bond pairs. Sodium chloride kept as the worked ionic example; magnesium oxide, methane and the dot-and-cross drawing rules dropped to stay inside 15 and avoid diagram-dependent cards.
